A1.justification: Both PDFs describe LaViDa-R1 and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–D. All 28 pages in each version support comparison, including the qualitative examples.

before.justification: v1 reports original LaViDa-R1 benchmark results, training ablations, reward trajectories, and qualitative outputs in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds evaluations on MMMU, MMBench, and MME in Table 3.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Appendix A retain the same unified SFT/GRPO/self-distillation objective, answer forcing, tree search, and complementary-masking likelihood estimator. No algorithmic or model component changes.

E1.justification: Section 4.2 adds evaluations on MMMU, MMBench, and MME, described as less reasoning-intensive multimodal understanding benchmarks. MMMU is additional to the retained MMMU-Pro evaluation. This extends existing visual-understanding coverage without changing training datasets or introducing a new task family.

E2.justification: New Table 3 includes LLaDa-V as a reported comparator alongside MMaDa and LaViDa-O. LLaDa-V was cited but had no reported comparison scores in v1. Comparator membership in the retained experiments is unchanged.

E3.justification: The stated training and evaluation settings in Section 4.1 and Appendix B.1 remain unchanged, including model size, training budgets, rewards, and generation lengths. The additional benchmark table does not document a separate change to splits, preprocessing, metric definitions, or testing procedures.

E4.justification: The answer-forcing, tree-search, likelihood-estimator, loss-mixture, and timestep-weighting ablations are retained with the same evidence. Appendix qualitative examples and the text-to-image reward-model case study also remain unchanged; Table 3 adds benchmark scores rather than a new diagnostic analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Table 3 continues the existing practice of reporting point scores.

E6.justification: v2 newly reports LaViDa-R1 scores of 47.0, 79.2, and 501 on MMMU, MMBench, and MME, respectively, versus LaViDa-O's 45.1, 76.4, and 488. LLaDa-V scores 48.6, 82.9, and 491, exceeding LaViDa-R1 on the first two benchmarks. These are additional results; existing numerical results and qualitative findings are retained.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulations and Appendix A derivations are unchanged in substance. Equation (2) drops the expectation subscript, a notation edit that does not alter the stated objective or introduce a new assumption or theoretical argument.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about unified multimodal reasoning, stable post-training, guided rollouts, and likelihood estimation. The additional benchmarks support existing claims without redefining them.

C2.justification: The explanations of training stability, performance gains, and failure conditions are retained. Appendix C preserves the limitations concerning autoregressive-model performance, inference infrastructure, task scope, and text-to-image rewards. The added benchmark paragraph reports a performance trend without a new mechanism explanation or substantive qualification.

D1.justification: Appendices A and B retain the same implementation details, dataset preparation, hyperparameters, hardware, training times, and inference instructions. The training-configuration table is merely renumbered from Table 8 to Table 9; no new code or data access information is supplied.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for MMMU (Yue et al., 2024), MMBench (Liu et al., 2024), and MME (Fu et al., 2023). The related-work discussion and research positioning in Section 2 and Appendix D otherwise remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 adds a short benchmark paragraph and acknowledgements, changes author ordering and corresponding-author information, and replaces the preprint notice with conference publication information. The narrative and section organization remain largely intact.

P2.justification: v2 inserts Table 3, renumbers subsequent tables, and moves Figure 5 from page 8 to page 9. These additions cause localized text and reference reflow; existing plots, diagrams, and qualitative images retain their content.

improvement.justification: Section 4.2 and new Table 3 modestly strengthen empirical validation by testing three additional multimodal benchmarks and including LLaDa-V as a comparator. The original experiments and appendix evidence are preserved. Limited benchmark-specific protocol detail and unchanged uncertainty reporting constrain the strength of this additional evidence.
